The scans#

This page covers both advisory scans Booster runs with plan, how to run either one alone, the audit run adds, and the dynamic-properties list on the PHP 8.2 step. Next: The dependency check.

The PHPCompatibility scan#

plan ends with an advisory scan: PHP_CodeSniffer runs the PHPCompatibility standard over the app and asks what will break on the PHP version the first PHP hop lands on. The findings are hints for the person doing the upgrade, never a gate: they do not change the exit code, and a scan that cannot run (missing tooling, a crash) is reported as "could not run" while the plan still prints in full. --no-scan skips both advisory scans.

The scan needs no change to the app: Booster ships PHP_CodeSniffer and the PHPCompatibility standard with its own dependencies, from the PHAR and from a clone alike. Booster looks for a PHP_CodeSniffer that carries the standard, trying the app's own vendor/bin/phpcs, then Booster's vendor/bin/phpcs, then phpcs on the PATH. When it runs Booster's own copy, it points PHP_CodeSniffer at the bundled standard with --runtime-set installed_paths, because the registration file that Composer's installer plugin writes cannot be trusted inside a PHAR unpacked into a temp directory. When none of the launchers has the standard, the scan reports a skip and the plan goes on; the skip says to reinstall Booster's dependencies (composer install in Booster's folder) or download the PHAR again.

The scan ignores vendor/, node_modules/ and storage/, because those hold third-party code and generated files, not the app's. It reads the app only and changes nothing. booster scan --path=../my-app --php=<target> runs the same scan on its own, for any PHP version Booster knows, and exits 0 even when it finds a wall of removed functions. If the app's composer.json declares ext-oci8 (in require, require-dev or config.platform), the scan leaves out the "oci_*() is removed since PHP 8.4" findings: PHP 8.4 moved oci8 out of the PHP download and into PECL, and an app that declares the extension installs the PECL one on purpose, so those lines would be false alarms. An app that deploys on Citadel gets the same treatment: when its Squire kit (.env.squire.example, .env.squire or docker-compose.squire.yml) names citadel/php-apache, the scan leaves those findings out too, because every Citadel PHP image installs oci8 from PECL, and the report says how many it left out and why. With neither, the findings stay, with a hint that they mean "install the PECL extension", not "Oracle support is gone". An oci_*() function removed before 8.4 (such as oci_internal_debug(), dropped in PHP 8.0) is gone from the PECL extension too, so that finding always stays, as does every other one. In an app that requires Pest (pestphp/pest), the scan also leaves out the "Closures / anonymous functions only have access to $this if used within a class" warning for files under tests/: Pest binds every test closure to a test case, so $this in it() and test() is the test case, and the warning fired on every test. In a Laravel app it is left out for routes/console.php too, whose closures Laravel binds to their command. The same warning anywhere else stays.

The PHPStan scan#

plan ends with a second advisory scan: PHPStan runs over the app at the destination PHP version, using Pinstripe's base.neon preset. The findings are hints for the person doing the upgrade, never a gate: they do not change the exit code, and a scan that cannot run is reported with the fix that enables it, while the plan still prints in full. --no-scan skips it.

The scan needs no change to the app: Booster ships PHPStan and Pinstripe's preset with its own dependencies, from the PHAR and from a clone alike. Booster looks for a PHPStan binary, trying the app's own vendor/bin/phpstan, then Booster's vendor/bin/phpstan, then phpstan on the PATH, and for the preset it tries the app's vendor tree and Booster's. When either is missing, the report says to reinstall Booster's dependencies (composer install in Booster's folder) or download the PHAR again.

It ignores vendor/, node_modules/ and storage/, reads the app only and changes nothing. booster scan --path=../my-app --php=8.5 --phpstan runs the same scan on its own, for any PHP version Booster knows, and exits 0 even when it finds a wall of missing types. In an app that requires Pest, "Call to an undefined method Pest..." findings under tests/ are left out: Pest's higher-order tests (it('...')->get('/')) call through magic proxies such as TestCall that PHPStan cannot follow.

The composer audit during the run#

run carries a third advisory check, per hop: after a hop changes composer.json or composer.lock, Booster runs composer audit --format=json --no-interaction in the app and lists advisories and abandoned packages in the step's report with counts. It never changes the exit code, a clean audit says Composer audit: clean (no advisories, no abandoned packages)., and a hop that changed no composer file skips it and says so. A dry run previews the hops and runs no audit.

Composer's audit exits 1 for advisories, 2 for abandoned packages and 3 for both. Booster reads the JSON report on every one of those exits, so an app with abandoned packages gets the list, not a "could not run". Only an exit with no JSON report behind it (Composer missing, a crash) is reported as "could not run".

Dynamic properties#

PHP 8.2 deprecates dynamic properties: assigning $this->name in a class that never declares $name. The plan step that crosses PHP 8.2 reads the app's own classes (it skips vendor/, node_modules/ and storage/) and lists every such assignment as file:line Class::$prop, or says how many classes it read and found none. run repeats them on that step as MANUAL lines. Booster never changes them: declare each property in its class, or mark the class #[\AllowDynamicProperties].

A class that declares the property in a parent or a trait, has a __set(), or already carries #[\AllowDynamicProperties] is not listed. A class whose parent or trait lives outside the app's own code (a library in vendor/) cannot be checked from the app alone, so it is named on a "not checked" line for you to check by hand. plan --format=json carries the same list under dynamic_properties.
